subject: MSA redline: Ariba PO schema validation & supplier token mapping
messages:
From: Danielle Myers <danielle.myers@acme-corp.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement-support@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-06-30 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO field validation & MSA redline impact on Ariba setup

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Legal ran the redlined MSA internally and noticed the change to Section 5 (Acceptance & PO Requirements) — specifically the removal of a hard requirement around line-level 'costCenterCode' in the order acknowledgment. Our Ariba enrollment team needs to understand whether Redwood will still emit a stable PO schema with the following required fields: PO#, lineNumber, sku/partNumber, unitPrice, quantity, shipToParty, and costCenterCode.

If the MSA language now relies on a downstream order form to capture billing routing, we need a commitment on the portal side so our supplier portal validation doesn't block EDI/PO acceptance.

Can you share: 1) representative PO XML we should expect from Redwood, and 2) any constraints you need on our Ariba field mapping so we can complete supplier registration? I attached our sample PO format for reference (acme_sample_po.xml).

We'd like to keep onboarding moving — can we get confirmation by end of day so procurement config isn't delayed?

Thanks,
Danielle
Danielle Myers
Sr. Supplier Onboarding Manager
Acme Corporation
procurement@acme-corp.com

--- Attachment: acme_sample_po.xml (XML stub) ---

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Myers <danielle.myers@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-30 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO field validation & MSA redline impact on Ariba setup

Danielle — thanks for the clear summary and the sample PO. Looping in Marissa (legal) for the MSA questions and Karthik (product/ops) for the Ariba field mapping specifics.

Quick answers up front:
- We continue to support a stable PO XML with the fields you listed.
- "costCenterCode" is optional at MSA level today but our supplier portal offers configurable required-fields per account; we can toggle costCenterCode as required for Acme to avoid manual rejections.

Pending: Marissa to confirm the contract-side commitment we can make as a formal representation. Karthik, can you confirm anything in the runtime that would strip or normalize the costCenterCode tag? Also attaching the redlined MSA we circulated internally (redwood_msa_redline_v3.docx).

If we can align on two options (1) require costCenterCode at portal validation, or (2) accept missing costCenterCode but require billing routing via order form metadata, how do you prefer to proceed?

Thanks,
Logan
Logan Wright
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
loganw@redwood.ai

--- Attachment: redwood_msa_redline_v3.docx (MSA redline stub) ---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Danielle Myers <danielle.myers@acme-corp.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-30 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO field validation & MSA redline impact on Ariba setup

Hi all,

I reviewed the redline and the specific deletion in Section 5. Legal is comfortable with two pragmatic pathways that keep procurement moving without creating an exposure for Redwood:

1) Operational commitment: Redwood will ensure the supplier portal enforces a required costCenterCode at ingestion for Acme's tenant during the supplier enrollment process. This is an ops-level control, not a contractual warranty; we can include operational language in the onboarding SOW/order form ("Redwood will configure supplier validation rules for Acme's portal to require costCenterCode on incoming PO documents").

2) Contractual fallback: If Acme prefers contractual language, we can insert a limited representation in the Order Form that an accepted PO will contain line-level billing routing fields, but that must be scoped as a non-indemnity representation. Legal prefers the operational route for speed.

Action items for Acme: confirm whether tenant-level portal validation (option 1) is acceptable. If yes, Procurement can complete field mapping without further redlines. If Acme insists on option 2, we will need a short order-form amendment (1 paragraph) and a loop to Finance for billing alignment.

I've attached a suggested one-paragraph amendment and an Excel mapping template (ariba_field_mapping_sheet.xlsx) to capture field names and expected XML paths. Logan / Karthik: product note — if we enforce costCenterCode at ingestion, ensure downstream tokenization for supplier tokens doesn't drop that element for ACKs.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132

--- Attachment: ariba_field_mapping_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet stub) ---

From: Greg Lowe <greg.lowe@acme-corp.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Danielle Myers <danielle.myers@acme-corp.com>, procurement-support@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-06-30 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PO field validation & MSA redline impact on Ariba setup

Thanks, Logan and Marissa. Acme is OK with option 1 (tenant-level portal validation) to keep the onboarding timeline. We'll mark costCenterCode as required in our Ariba mapping and validate against the sample PO. I've attached an updated sample PO with the supplier-specific element we use (acme_sample_po.xml) — same file as before with a note on the cost center path.

Next steps for Redwood:
- Karthik, please confirm whether your ingestion layer will accept the Acme path for costCenterCode without rewriting it.
- Logan/Marissa: once Karthik confirms, we'll proceed to register the supplier in Ariba and kick off test POs next week.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Greg
Gregory Lowe
Senior Director, Procurement Systems
Acme Corporation
greg.lowe@acme-corp.com
